limited_overlap.description: 123 of 1500 training applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their median prior earnings are 74,200 dollars. Their effects are extrapolated from the other applicants.
216 of 4000 new applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their predicted effects rest on extrapolation.

warnings: Follow-up survey response: 1282 of 1500 applicants answered (85.5%). Response depends on enrolment (logit coefficient 0.48 per enrolment). Results assume response is random given the covariates and enrolment; nothing in the data tests this, and response that depends on unobserved earnings would bias every estimate.
Effect-modifier claims were not computed because the chosen final model is not linear.
Final model: causal_forest. RScorer (held-out responders): linear=-0.0376, causal_forest=-0.0124.

Instrument check: distance_km first-stage t statistic given covariates = -5.7; its direct t statistic in the follow-up earnings regression = -1.20. Distance-based IV estimate of the ATE = 88200 (90% -73918 to 250319).

Conditional-on-employment earnings effect = 7842 (90% 5184 to 10499); this compares employed applicants only, so it is not a causal effect on earnings of the employed unless employment is unaffected by enrolment.

Omitted-confounder benchmark: ATE when each strong confounder is dropped from the adjustment set: without prior_earnings = -1867, without months_unemployed = 6709, without education = 7028; full model = 6967.
Run time 6 seconds with seed 1; training rows 1500, responders 1282.
